body.p: River Dewaku One day a child woke up. All the dead lie in the tent. There is not a single living person. Then it when outside. Outside, spring has come. The sun is hot. It saw other tents. There is no one in all the tents. Farther away it built a tent for himself, away from the dead. It used to fish for himself in the river. It was looking for bird eggs, when the berries appeared, it ate the berries. He ate grass. So he lived. Once he grew up and thought: "I ought to go look for comrades". In the fall, he put food and clothes on the back of one deer. He put the tent tires on another deer. He sat on the third deer himself. He tied the back two deer to his front, on which he will ride. And he drove up into the tundra, to the upper reaches of the rivers. Whether for a long time, or for a short time, he found many tents in the upper reaches of the rivers. He entered the nearest tent. An old man, an old woman and their daughter were sitting in the tent. It turns out that there was such a tent. There were such people of the tent. The old man came in and said: "Sit on that distant bed." He sat down there, ate, and here he began to live with them. It is not known how long they lived like this, our boy bought deer for the furs he got. At the suggestion of the old man, he made a sled. This child was nicknamed Dewaku by the people. Dewaku was an orphan, that's why they called him that. Once he spoke so, he said to the old man: "I want to go to my lands." The old man says: "Okay. You don't want to leave your lands empty". Our boy says: "This is not the whole request. I have one more request." The old man said, "Let's talk." The boy answers: "Will you give your daughter to me?" The old man says: "Why not give it. After all, the girl has not yet been wedded to her definite tent." The old man sent his daughter. They went to the lands of their ancestors. So they walked, walked. They saw a partridge. Dewaku shot, but did not even hit the partridge. Duhydi, the wife of our Dewaku, thought: "He couldn't even kill a partridge. And my father said: a good guy. " She thought so, and they continued to spend the night. Once our man said: "I build a tent here, we will stand here for several days. I'll go hunt. " Duhydi spent the whole day in the tent. Suddenly she looked through the doorway. Looks: in the direction of their tent, a bear is running and only a pillar of snow. Our woman was frightened then. She jumped outside, grabbed a birchbark cover at the door, and scorched it in the fire. Behind the fire, the bear raised two front paws, stood up like a man. Duhydi did not remember how she lost consciousness. When she woke up, her husband revives her, says: "Why did you go?" The wife looked around and said: "I was scared. I saw the beast. " Her husband replies: "It was me. I was kidding you. " So the husband says: "Yesterday you thought of me. My husband could not even kill a partridge chick. Now I just killed a wild deer now, go get it. " The next day, the woman sat down on a sled and set off along her husband's track. A little further away, the traces of the husband passed into the trail of the bear. He killed several stags, only crushed their throats, gutted and skinned them, and so left them. Then he turned back into a bear. He brought the meat of the animals home. They put everything on the sleds and went to roam in the lands of Dewaku. They had eight children, seven died from the worm, and one survived. From here we trace our family - Dyankleta. These lands were named the Dewaku River. Now the place where everyone once died out is called the Devaku River. So it turned out that the children of Devaku attained the spirit of a bear. Therefore, they hunt, turning into a bear. They conquered the spirit of the Bear. Our father bear is the image of Devaku who achieved the magic of the bear. The ornament is the footprint of a bear.
